summary: A seventeen-year-old narrator describes how Microsoft's Xbox countermeasures block unlicensed software, and how online gaming has become full of predators, undercover cops and monitors enforcing Terms of Service. He distributes ParanoidXbox game discs, which are unmonitored and spread via sneakernet and copying under the name Xnet, reaching Oakland within two weeks. The story also touches on classroom surveillance cameras and BART's switch to RFID contactless cards, which make him feel tracked.
one_line: A teenager's account of unmonitored ParanoidXbox game discs spreading as the Xnet network, amid surveillance in games, schools and transit.
key_facts: Razor-blade companies like Microsoft make it hard and/or illegal to compete with them on the blades, producing an 80 percent profit margin.
Every Xbox has had countermeasures to keep users from running software released by people who did not pay Microsoft for the right to sell Xbox programs.
The narrator is a seventeen year old boy.
Online game Terms of Service said no flirting, no cussing, and no "clear or masked language which insultingly refers to any aspect of sexual orientation or sexuality."
No one monitored the ParanoidXbox games because they were not run by a company but were games hackers had written for the hell of it.
A group of parents sued the school board over surveillance cameras in classrooms but had already lost their bid for a preliminary injunction against them.
The name Xnet was used by people talking about it on the Muni, and the name stuck.
Discs the narrator started distributing last week were sneakernetted and copied all the way to Oakland in the space of two weeks.
The BART had completely abandoned cash fares in favor of arphid "contactless" cards waved at turnstiles.
The narrator felt he was being tracked every time he used a BART contactless card.
Someone on Xnet posted a link to an Electronic Frontier Foundation white paper.
Van called the narrator to ask whether he had heard of Xnet, and he nearly choked when he realized what she meant.
A message from Mandy said, "I'm lactose intolerant."
